$comment: What 1 January 1972 was, written against the period and not against the scenario module. If this and atlas/scenarios/cold_war.py disagree, one of them is wrong and somebody has to decide which -- do not edit this into agreement.
sources: Treaty texts and membership as they stood on 1 January 1972: the North Atlantic Treaty (15 parties, Greece and Turkey since 1952, the Federal Republic since 1955), the Warsaw Treaty (7 -- Albania stopped participating in 1968), UN Security Council composition for the 1972 term, SIPRI/NRDC arsenal figures scaled to this engine's warhead unit, and the ratification calendar of the Ostpolitik treaties.

alliances.name: North Atlantic Treaty
alliances.because: fifteen parties in 1972. France left the integrated military command in 1966 and never left the treaty, so it is a party. Spain is not -- it acceded in 1982.

alliances.name: Warsaw Treaty
alliances.because: seven. Albania stopped participating after the invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968 and is not a party; Yugoslavia never was.

alliances.name: US-ROK Mutual Defense Treaty
alliances.because: 1953, and two American divisions on the peninsula.

alliances.name: USSR-DPRK Treaty of Friendship
alliances.because: 1961. Pyongyang holds both and honours neither exclusively -- both must exist for that to be playable.

organisations.because: fifteen seats since the 1965 enlargement -- five permanent, ten elected. The permanent five are the victors of 1945; China's seat passed to the People's Republic in October 1971, three months before this world begins.

dependencies.name: West Berlin
dependencies.because: an occupied city under three Western garrisons, not a Land of the Federal Republic and not East German ground. Held by the United States here because the engine has one holder per region and the American garrison is the one the guarantee runs through.

dependencies.name: British Honduras
dependencies.because: British until 1981, and not a state called Belize.

cores.because: East Berlin is the capital of the German Democratic Republic and its own ground.
the two Vietnams are each other's claim and neither is the other's core -- if Saigon were a northern core the engine would read reunification as recovery.
held by the United States and American ground in no sense at all. A colony or a garrison is not a core, and the day it becomes one a peace settlement has no way to hand it back.

ungoverned.because: the Antarctic Treaty of 1961. Nobody's state, and better modelled as ground with no government than as a nation with a treasury and a border guard on the ice.

not_yet.name: Eritrea
not_yet.because: federated then annexed to Ethiopia; independent 1993

not_yet.name: Zimbabwe
not_yet.because: Rhodesia in 1972, and on this map it is called that

not_yet.name: Namibia
not_yet.because: South West Africa, administered by South Africa until 1990

not_yet.name: Belize
not_yet.because: British Honduras; the name changes in 1973 and independence comes in 1981

leaders.name: Emilio Colombo
leaders.title: Presidente del Consiglio
leaders.because: Colombo's government fell in January 1972 and Andreotti's first followed in February. On 1 January it is still Colombo.

leaders.name: Edward Gierek
leaders.title: First Secretary
leaders.because: Gierek replaced Gomulka after the December 1970 shootings.

leaders.name: Lê Duẩn
leaders.title: First Secretary
leaders.because: Ho Chi Minh died in 1969; Le Duan is the one running the war.

treaties.name: Treaty of Moscow
treaties.because: signed August 1970 and ratified in May 1972. On 1 January it is signed and not in force, and the difference is whether the engine can report it broken.

treaties.name: Treaty of Warsaw
treaties.because: signed December 1970, ratified May 1972 in the same Bundestag fight.

treaties.name: Four Power Agreement on Berlin
treaties.because: signed September 1971; the final protocol bringing it into force is June 1972.

treaties.name: Korean Armistice
treaties.because: in force since 1953 and never replaced by a peace.

treaties.name: Rogers ceasefire
treaties.because: August 1970, holding along the canal, and the thing October 1973 breaks.

treaties.name: Comecon
treaties.because: the same seven as the Warsaw Treaty, which is the point: the bloc is one thing with two instruments.

arsenals.because: bombers, Minuteman, and Polaris/Poseidon boats -- all three legs.
behind on warheads, ahead on throw-weight, and all three legs by 1972.
Polaris in four Resolution boats and nothing else -- the V-force gave up the strategic role in 1969. Two of the three modelled hulls carry it.
the Plateau d'Albion silos are the force in 1972; Le Redoutable had been operational for three weeks.
bombs on H-6 bombers. No Chinese ballistic-missile submarine went to sea until 1981, so the count is nought and says so rather than leaving it implied by the tier.
undeclared, deliverable by aircraft, and no submarine leg for another quarter-century.

delivery.because: the two powers whose whole arsenal is carried by aircraft. Six hops is a combat radius: your own theatre and its neighbours, not the far side of the planet. Walked on this world's adjacency, so the boundary tested is the one a warhead meets.

silent_on.occupied: No ground begins under an occupation it does not own. The Cold War's occupations had all been converted into sovereignty or into a dependency by 1972 -- East Germany is a state, West Berlin is a dependency, and neither is modelled as occupied ground.

doctrines.because: the draft did not end until 1973; in January 1972 this is a conscript army
all-volunteer since national service ended in 1963
Polaris: four boats, one at sea
the force de frappe; dissuasion du faible au fort
no first use, declared with the first test in 1964
the Non-Aligned Movement, which India led
the Self-Defense Forces: small and entirely volunteer
